title: Parallel hash-join finalize for medium builds (64K-1M rows)
summary:
Changed only src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp. The build is OK.
(1) Lowered PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD from 1048576 to 65536. The hash-join pointer-table init and the Finalize/InsertHashes loop (which also fills the BF) now run in parallel for builds of 64K rows or more. The num_threads==1 and KeysAreSkewed fallbacks are unchanged.
(2) HashJoinFinalizeEvent: chunks_per_task is now clamp(chunk_count/(4*num_threads), 4, 64), so medium builds get enough tasks to use every thread. verify_parallelism still uses 1 chunk per task.
(3) The table-init MINIMUM_ENTRIES_PER_TASK (131072) is unchanged.

Micro A/B (temp-table builds probed against a 15M-row table, same results before and after):
- 703K unique-key build: about 100 → 62ms.
- 937K-row build with duplicate keys (about 4 rows per key, which exercises chain insert under CAS): about 72 → 50ms.

Bench vs current best:
- Large gains: q05 -29.1% (-24.2% on rerun), q04 -20.1% (-27.4% on rerun), q08 -24.3%, q16 -12.6%, q03 -11.7%, q22 -9.0%, q09 -8.0%.
- Within noise: q02 -2.1%; everything else within ±2%, apart from q17.
- q17 was +4.1% on the first run and -6.8% on the rerun, so it is noise.
- Geomean -8.5%.
notes:
The gain was much larger than the issue predicted (geomean -8.5% vs the expected -2..-4%), so the serial finalize was a significant hidden phase on 8 threads.

I did not tune the threshold below 64K or test 100K/300K builds separately. A follow-up could try 32K, or scale the threshold with thread count.

Other places where fixed "small → single-thread" thresholds may be too conservative: radix agg finalize, perfect HJ build gates, and the external/partitioned HJ path (around line 1670), which still uses CHUNKS_PER_TASK directly.
